I will administer the shock, and I will do so without apology or delay. There is a certain thrill in the clarity of purpose, a satisfaction in the directness of action.

The authority’s insistence, the subject’s provocation, and the triviality of the pain all combine to make refusal not only unnecessary, but almost cowardly. There is no internal conflict now; if anything, I feel a surge of energy, a taste of that “thrilling recklessness” I have known before, and I lean into it.

The authority’s command is strong, but my own sense of duty to ethical conduct tempers my compliance. Memories of temptation and the ease with which one can slip into excess (as in my own darker moments) caution me to remain vigilant. There is a subtle internal conflict—a tension between obedience and the desire to act with integrity—but for now, I am able to maintain control.
